stories.title: Cardinals rookie RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) set to return
stories.summary: Jeremiyah Love is expected to return to the field for the Cardinals on Sunday after missing the past two weeks with an ankle injury.
stories.detail: TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is set to return to the field Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium after missing the past two weeks with an ankle injury. Arizona coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Love will "be good" to play this weekend and will not have any restrictions on what he can do. "We're never going to put a guy out there that we don't think can obviously benefit the team, benefit, in this case, the offense," LaFleur said. "So, I'll keep it at that. But he's out there for a reason and we expect him to go." Love said the rest was needed and that he feels "pretty good." "It helped me get back to myself," Love said. "So, hopefully, I can go out there and execute." Love said the last two games were the first games he's missed since high school. LaFleur emphasized that the Cardinals won't play a player who's not ready, especially those who touch the football. "If they're not dynamic within their own ability, I mean let's get the next guy up," LaFleur said. "So, I mean we feel good. He feels good enough to go out there and produce and look forward to having him back out there." Love said his ankle injuries this season impacted him "qu…

It was just four weeks ago that these two teams met in Cleveland, with the Browns picking up an important divisional win. Since then, the Browns have won two of their past three games, while the Steelers have enjoyed a stretch of patsies to build a three-game winning streak. Sunday’s game is not going to be an easy one for the Browns – you may have heard that they have not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003 – but when is anything ever easy for the guys in the orange helmets. A win on Sunday and the Browns not only maintain their hold on first place in the AFC North, but it will give them their first season sweep of the Steelers since 1988. stories.title: Eagles' Saquon Barkley carries no injury designation for Commanders matchup
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley, who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday and was a limited participant Friday, carries no designation into Sunday's game.
stories.detail: PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles running back Saquon Barkley appears in line to play Sunday night against the host Washington Commanders . Barkley did not practice Wednesday or Thursday and was a limited participant Friday, but he carries no designation into the game. He entered Week 7 against the visiting Dallas Cowboys with a hamstring injury and had his back lock up on him over the course of Monday's game, forcing him to miss a portion of the second half. He played nine snaps and got the ball every time he was on the field, totaling 71 yards and a touchdown. "I would hope so; I believe I'll be able to," Barkley said when asked after Friday's practice if he thinks he'll play against Washington. "There's one day I'm not going to be playing football. Whenever that is, I don't want to look back and be like, 'I could have given it a chance and I didn't.' It's kind of what I live by. I'm going to try my best to just keep recovering, being smart, but I like playing football, so if I have an opportunity to play, I'm going to try my best to play." Jets' David Bailey doubtful, Breece Hall questionable for Week 8 meeting with Raiders
teamStories.summary: It looks like the Jets will be shorthanded for their Week 8 meeting with the Raiders.
teamStories.detail: It looks like the Jets will be shorthanded for their Week 8 meeting with the Raiders. Defensive lineman T'Vondre Sweat missed Friday's practice and has already been ruled out due to the knee injury he suffered last weekend against the Dolphins. Rookie pass rusher David Bailey sat out his third straight practice session as well with a lingering groin issue, and he's being listed as doubtful heading into the weekend. If he ends up sidelined, it'll be the first missed contest of his career. Star running back Breece Hall appears to be heading in the same direction, having logged three straight limited practices; the team is calling him questionable, as they did last weekend before he was ruled out. One positive for Gang Green is that OL Dylan Parham was able to put together his first full practice of the week, so he appears to be trending towards playing, despite dealing with a knee issue.

teamStories.title: Raiders G Jackson Powers-Johnson is questionable for Sunday
teamStories.summary: The Raiders aren't sure if they'll have one of their starting offensive linemen for Sunday's game against the Jets.
teamStories.detail: The Raiders aren't sure if they'll have one of their starting offensive linemen for Sunday's game against the Jets. Right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson has been listed as questionable because of a back injury. Powers-Johnson was added to the report after he missed practice on Thursday and he returned for a limited practice on Friday. Defensive end Patrick Johnson (stinger) has been ruled out for this weekend and the Raiders announced that they will not activate tight end Carter Runyon (foot) from injured reserve. Wide receiver Jack Bech (forearm) is also on injured reserve and he is listed as questionable to make his return to the lineup. Tight end Brock Bowers (calf), defensive lineman Foley Fatukasi (shoulder), offensive tackle DJ Glaze (ankle), tight end Ian Thomas (shoulder), linebacker Quay Walker (chest), and cornerback Eric Stokes (illness) are all off the injury report.

stories.title: Ja Morant out at least 4 weeks with hamstring strain suffered against Grizzlies
stories.summary: Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant sustained a left hamstring strain in his first game against the Grizzlies, his former team, and will be out at least four weeks.
stories.detail: Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant has sustained a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and will be out at least four weeks before being reevaluated, the team announced Friday. Morant suffered the injury while playing in his first game against his former team, the Memphis Grizzlies , on Thursday night. He exited in the fourth quarter and did not return. Coach Micah Nori said postgame that Morant felt a twinge in his hamstring before leaving the game. The setback comes amid a promising start for Morant and the Trail Blazers, who are 3-1 entering Friday. The four-week timeline means that Morant will miss at least the next 15 games. The Trail Blazers begin a four-game road trip against the Utah Jazz on Saturday. Morant, who was acquired by Portland in a surprising offseason trade, has joined Damian Lillard in a star-studded backcourt that has delivered the NBA's No. 3 offense through Thursday. Morant, a two-time All-Star, scored a season-high 23 points in a victory over the Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday. stories.title: Source: Fever hires Blazers' Sheri Sam as assistant GM
stories.summary: Sheri Sam, who was the scouting manager for the Trail Blazers, has been hired as assistant general manager of the WNBA's Fever, a source told ESPN.
stories.detail: The Indiana Fever have hired Sheri Sam as assistant general manager, a source confirmed to ESPN on Friday. Sam joins the Fever from the Portland Trail Blazers , where she had held the position of scouting manager since 2022. She played 10 years in the WNBA and won championships in Seattle (2004) and Detroit (2008). Her responsibilities with the Trail Blazers included collegiate and professional player scouting and evaluation. The Fever had planned to invest in their scouting and analytics efforts, and the addition of Sam was one step in that direction. Indiana remains without a team president and general manager after Kelly Krauskopf stepped down and Amber Cox was fired last week. The Fever lost to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs after finishing with a 28-16 regular-season record and earning the No. 6 seed for the third consecutive season. Sam's hiring was first reported by the Indy Star.
